questions.question: What is the difference between instance and class methods?
questions.title: Instance vs Class Methods
questions.direct_answer: Instance methods operate on an instance (its @vars); class methods operate on the class itself. `d.bark` (instance) uses d's @name; `Dog.count` (class) uses @@count. Define instance with `def bark`; define class with `def self.count` (or class << self). Instance methods are called on objects (Dog.new.bark); class methods on the class (Dog.count). Instance methods see @x (per-object state); class methods see @@x / class state (not @x — there's no instance). Use instance methods for behavior of one object; class methods for factories, utilities, counters, and config that don't need an instance. Inside an instance method, `self` is the instance; inside a class method, `self` is the class. A class method can't directly call an instance method (no instance) unless it creates one (new).

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know instance methods act on an instance (@x) and class methods act on the class (@@x, no instance).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Calling a class method on an instance (or vice versa), or accessing @x from a class method.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Instance methods = on objects (d.bark, see @x). Class methods = on the class (Dog.count, see @@x, not @x). def self.m vs def m.

sections.title: Instance vs class methods
sections.content:
```ruby
class Dog
  @@count = 0                      # CLASS variable (shared)

  def initialize(name)
    @name = name                    # INSTANCE variable (per-object)
    @@count += 1
  end

  # INSTANCE method: on an object, sees @x
  def bark;     "#{@name} says Woof"; end
  def name;    @name; end

  # CLASS method: on the class, sees @@x (NOT @x)
  def self.count;      @@count; end
  def self.describe;    'a Dog class'; end
end

d = Dog.new('Rex')
e = Dog.new('Buddy')

# INSTANCE methods -> called on OBJECTS
d.bark        # 'Rex says Woof'
d.name        # 'Rex'  (sees d's @name)

# CLASS methods -> called on the CLASS
Dog.count     # 2  (sees @@count)
Dog.describe  # 'a Dog class'

# Don't mix the call sites:
# d.count        # NoMethodError (count is a class method)
# Dog.bark       # NoMethodError (bark is an instance method)

# `self` differs by context:
class Dog
  def whoami;      self; end       # self = the INSTANCE (d)
  def self.whoami; self; end       # self = the CLASS (Dog)
end
d.whoami       # #<Dog:...>  (the instance)
Dog.whoami     # Dog          (the class)

# Class method CAN'T see @x (no instance):
# def self.name; @name; end  -> always nil (no instance)
# It can create one: def self.make; new('x'); end
```

Inside an instance method, `self` is the instance; inside a class method, `self` is the class. A class method can't directly call an instance method (no instance) unless it creates one (new). Once I find the first incorrect state, I would make the smallest fix, add a regression test, and run the boundary cases. I would also check the change under realistic load before calling it done.

sections.title: Understand the decision
sections.content:
Instance methods operate on an instance (its @vars); class methods operate on the class itself.

`d.bark` (instance) uses d's @name; `Dog.count` (class) uses @@count.

Define instance with `def bark`; define class with `def self.count` (or class << self). Instance methods are called on objects (Dog.new.bark); class methods on the class (Dog.count). Instance methods see @x (per-object state); class methods see @@x / class state (not @x — there's no instance). Use instance methods for behavior of one object; class methods for factories, utilities, counters, and config that don't need an instance. Inside an instance method, `self` is the instance; inside a class method, `self` is the class.

A common mistake is calling a class method on an instance (or vice versa), or accessing @x from a class method.

sections.title: Instance vs class methods
sections.content:
```ruby
class Dog
  @@count = 0                      # CLASS variable (shared)

  def initialize(name)
    @name = name                    # INSTANCE variable (per-object)
    @@count += 1
  end

  # INSTANCE method: on an object, sees @x
  def bark;     "#{@name} says Woof"; end
  def name;    @name; end

  # CLASS method: on the class, sees @@x (NOT @x)
  def self.count;      @@count; end
  def self.describe;    'a Dog class'; end
end

d = Dog.new('Rex')
e = Dog.new('Buddy')

# INSTANCE methods -> called on OBJECTS
d.bark        # 'Rex says Woof'
d.name        # 'Rex'  (sees d's @name)

# CLASS methods -> called on the CLASS
Dog.count     # 2  (sees @@count)
Dog.describe  # 'a Dog class'

# Don't mix the call sites:
# d.count        # NoMethodError (count is a class method)
# Dog.bark       # NoMethodError (bark is an instance method)

# `self` differs by context:
class Dog
  def whoami;      self; end       # self = the INSTANCE (d)
  def self.whoami; self; end       # self = the CLASS (Dog)
end
d.whoami       # #<Dog:...>  (the instance)
Dog.whoami     # Dog          (the class)

# Class method CAN'T see @x (no instance):
# def self.name; @name; end  -> always nil (no instance)
# It can create one: def self.make; new('x'); end
```
